segments.prompt:
2D hand-drawn cinematic single-character sequence, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds.

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the exact identity, drawing language, proportions, materials and original colors of the approved Picture 1 mouse-ear mutant girl references. Keep her white short hair with eye-covering fringe and small upward curl, large translucent pale-violet mouse-ear mutation structures, small slender body, oversized pale short robe, dark collar, cuffs and hem blocks, diagonal strap, one side satchel, pale socks and oversized dark shoes. Preserve the verified identity, existing elements, spatial continuity and monochrome palette logic of Picture 2. Reference fidelity overrides generic style wording.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: use restrained readable 2D motion, compatible variable-weight linework, reference-consistent thin shading, soft diffuse light and generous quiet negative space only where compatible with the source images. The visual experiment is directional listening: the ear structures react first, then the eyes, while the body remains still. Do not impose colors or materials absent from the references.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show exactly one physical instance of the established mouse-ear mutant girl. The half-body dynamic sheet and full-body identity sheet describe the same one person, never four people. Keep both feet planted and use only small head, eye and ear movements.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): preserve SCENE-01 as the same forest-lake location with its registered monochrome hierarchy and single-path clarity. Picture 2 controls location identity and palette logic, not one mandatory crop. Use only visible, supported ground, water, tree layers, mist and open space. Do not invent a visible animal, person, machine, building, bridge, dock, sign, lamp or sound-producing object.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: one fixed eye-level medium-wide three-quarter view. Keep the whole character and both feet readable in the middle ground, with supported open ground in the foreground and forest-lake depth behind her. Place her slightly off center, leaving quiet negative space on both sides for the directional sound change. No push, pan, tilt, cut or axis change.

ACTION: begin with the girl standing quietly on the existing supported ground beside the forest lake, hands close to her robe and both feet still. A light natural breeze first moves the nearby leaves on screen-left; her screen-left mouse-ear structure turns a small angle toward that sound while the other ear remains neutral. The leaf sound fades and a soft water-lap becomes clearer on screen-right. Her screen-right ear then turns toward the water. Only after both ear reactions are readable do her eyes move from left to right; her head follows by a few degrees and stops between the two directions. End with her body and feet unchanged, listening rather than fleeing.

AUDIO DESIGN: quiet forest-lake air, one brief screen-left leaf rustle, a short near-silent gap, then soft screen-right water-lap and faint cloth settling. Use one very soft non-lyrical breath-like tone that begins after the second ear turns and fades when her head stops. Audio establishes direction and cautious attention; it is not a song, beat track or MV cue.

NEGATIVE: no second character, duplicate girl, clone, split screen, four-person character-sheet output, reflection person, shadow double or autonomous silhouette; no rabbit ears, ordinary replacement ears, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, new bag or changed robe; no visible animal or invented sound source; no walking, running, jumping, dancing, panic, exaggerated recoil or lip-sync; no camera movement, reframing, cut, axis flip or montage; no location replacement, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, cyan-white energy humanoid, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.

segments.prompt:

STYLE IDENTITY LOCK: preserve the exact same Picture 1 mouse-ear mutant girl, including face, white short hair, translucent pale-violet mouse-ear mutation structures, small slender proportions, oversized pale short robe, dark edge blocks, diagonal strap, single side satchel, socks and oversized dark shoes. Preserve the same Picture 2 forest-lake identity, existing elements, monochrome hierarchy, lighting direction and original palette logic. Reference fidelity overrides generic style wording.

VISUAL EXPRESSION VARIABLE: continue restrained readable 2D motion, compatible variable-weight linework, reference-consistent thin shading, soft diffuse light and quiet negative space. The decision becomes visible through a small sequence from ears to eyes to shoulders to one step. Do not add colors or materials that conflict with either reference.

CHARACTER (Picture 1): show the same one physical girl from Segment A. Inherit the selected real A ending pose, ear angles, head direction, clothing state and satchel position. Her four reference views remain one identity.

ENVIRONMENT (Picture 2): remain in the same SCENE-01 space and use only an existing visually supported direction along the ground. Maintain the same forest-lake layers and monochrome palette logic. If Picture 2 does not support a safe visible step direction, Work must not render this segment rather than inventing new terrain.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: keep the same fixed eye-level medium-wide three-quarter frame and the same spatial axis from Segment A. Preserve foreground open ground, the character in the middle ground and forest-lake depth behind her. The chosen step must stay inside the established frame. No camera movement or cut.

ACTION: from the held Segment A ending, the screen-left leaf rustle subsides while the screen-right water-lap remains soft and regular. Her two mouse-ear structures settle toward the quieter right-hand direction. Her eyes confirm that direction, then her head and shoulders align by a small amount. She shifts her weight without lifting both feet, slides the existing side satchel slightly closer with one forearm, and takes exactly one small step along the visually supported ground, parallel to the safe existing route rather than toward the water. The robe hem and satchel make one restrained follow-through and settle. End with both feet planted again, ears relaxed but attentive, and the same single character continuing calmly.

AUDIO DESIGN: continue the same forest-lake air and screen-right water-lap, add one soft cloth press at the satchel, one small footfall and a brief robe-and-strap settling sound. The breath-like non-lyrical tone opens slightly at the weight shift and resolves when both feet plant. Audio supports the decision and landing; it is not a song cue, beat-synced edit or MV structure.

NEGATIVE: no second character, duplicate girl, clone, split screen, four-person character-sheet output, reflection person, shadow double or autonomous silhouette; no rabbit ears, ordinary replacement ears, tail, horns, wings, armor, weapon, new bag or changed robe; no visible animal, person or invented sound source; no step toward or into water, extra steps, run, jump, dance, panic, exaggerated recoil or lip-sync; no camera movement, reframe, cut, axis flip, reverse terrain or montage; no invented bridge, dock, stones, roots, building, sign, lamp or path; no location replacement, glossy 3D render, hard synthetic digital edges, cyan-white energy humanoid, text, subtitle, logo or watermark.
